reader.summary: Indonesia's week was defined by the ongoing forest-fire and toxic-haze crisis, which a new report said killed 3,560 people in September alone. Rain eventually brought relief to Borneo and other affected areas, but the health toll and public frustration remained severe. Student-led protests erupted in multiple cities, with demonstrators demanding government action on both the wildfires and rising living costs; some chanted 'eat the rich' against graft. On the economic front, the MSCI downgrade warning continued to shake markets: Indonesian tycoons lost roughly 57 billion dollars, a corporate bond sale was shelved, the 10-year yield hit a four-year high, and the central bank moved to strengthen anti-manipulation rules while reassuring businesses. Prabowo's brother publicly sounded the alarm over the stock market. Diplomatically, Indonesia cut pipeline gas exports to Singapore by about nine percent, prompting a joint haze task force and a visit by Singapore's top envoy. Indonesia also secured a UAE oil-supply commitment of up to 30 million barrels and sent its energy minister to China and India to secure gasoline. An earthquake displaced nearly 13,000 people, and Thailand returned smuggled orangutans to Indonesia.

key_events.event: A new report found that wildfire smoke killed 3,560 people in Indonesia in September, underscoring the severe health toll of the haze crisis.
The MSCI downgrade warning triggered a market rout in which Indonesian tycoons lost roughly 57 billion dollars and a corporate bond sale was shelved.
Hundreds of students protested across Indonesia, demanding government action on wildfires, rising costs, and graft, with chants of 'eat the rich.'
Indonesia cut pipeline gas exports to Singapore by about nine percent, prompting a joint haze task force and a visit by Singapore's top envoy.
An earthquake in Indonesia displaced nearly 13,000 people.
Indonesia secured a UAE oil-supply commitment for up to 30 million barrels and sent its energy minister to China and India to ensure gasoline supply.
Indonesia's free-meals agency pledged urgent action after a wave of food-poisoning incidents linked to the programme.
Thailand returned smuggled orangutans to Indonesia, where a new sanctuary was set up for animals rescued from burning forests.
